name: Birzaith
overview: Birzaith was a male member of the tribe of Asher in ancient Israel. He is identified specifically as the son of Malchiel, establishing his place within the genealogical records of the tribe. Beyond this paternal link, there are no additional biblical notes or details about his life or actions.
namesAndTitles: The name Birzaith means 'well of olive oil,' a proper name recorded in 1 Chronicles 7:32. This name does not appear to be given directly by God but carries a meaning connected to olive oil, which in biblical symbolism often represents blessing and anointing.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Birzaith as the son of Malchiel, as noted in 1 Chronicles 7:31. No other family relationships or descendants are mentioned in the biblical text beyond this paternal connection.
scriptureSignificance: Birzaith's significance lies primarily in his inclusion in the genealogical listings of the tribe of Asher, which helped preserve the lineage and tribal identity of Israel. His mention as the son of Malchiel contributes to the biblical record of Israel's tribal families, underscoring the faithfulness of God in preserving His people through generations. While no direct narrative or actions are attributed to him, his presence in Scripture affirms the continuity of God's covenant people.
